questions.question: Which organisation oversees the development and standardisation of technologies for the World Wide Web?

• W3C's mission is to lead the Web to its full potential by developing protocols and guidelines that ensure long-term growth for the Web.
 
• W3C operates under an open and transparent process aimed at building consensus and ensuring high-quality standards.

• IEEE is responsible for setting technical standards in various fields but is not specific to the Web.
 
 
 
• **IEIT (Institution of Engineering and Technology)**
 
 
• IEIT is a multidisciplinary professional engineering institution.
 
• It works to inspire, inform, and influence the global engineering community.

• WHO is a specialized agency of the United Nations responsible for international public health.

questions.question: Which wireless technology allows devices to connect to the internet within the limited range of a wireless router?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Wi-Fi** stands for **Wireless Fidelity** and is a technology that allows devices to connect to the internet wirelessly within the range of a wireless router.
 
• It operates over radio waves, typically in the 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz bands, to transmit data.
 
• Wi-Fi is widely used in homes, offices, and public places like cafes and airports to provide internet access.
 
• Most modern devices, including smartphones, laptops, and tablets, are equipped with Wi-Fi capabilities to connect to wireless networks.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Wireless Router**

 
 
• A wireless router is a device that provides access to the internet or a private computer network.
 
• It uses radio waves to transmit data and can support multiple devices simultaneously.
 
• Most routers come with built-in security features like firewalls and encryption to protect the network.
 
 
 
• **Wi-Fi Standards**
 
 
• Wi-Fi standards are developed by the IEEE (Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers).
 
• Common standards include 802.11a, 802.11b, 802.11g, 802.11n, and 802.11ac, each offering different speeds and ranges.
 
 
 
• **Hotspot**
 
 
• A hotspot is a physical location where people can access the internet via Wi-Fi.
 
• Hotspots can be found in public places like cafes, airports, hotels, and libraries.
 
 
 
• **Internet Service Provider (ISP)**
 
 
• An ISP is a company that provides internet access to users.
 
• ISPs supply the necessary infrastructure, such as cables and routers, to connect users to the internet.

questions.question: Which Internet access technique uses the existing cable television infrastructure to provide high-speed Internet access to users?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1) Cable Internet**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cable Internet** utilizes the existing **cable television infrastructure** to provide high-speed Internet access to users.
 
• It operates by transmitting data over the **coaxial cables** that are used for cable television services.
 
• The service is typically provided by **cable television operators** who offer bundled packages that include both television and Internet services.
 
• **Cable modems** are used to connect the user's device to the cable network, enabling Internet access.
 
• This technology offers **high-speed data transfer rates**, making it suitable for activities such as streaming, gaming, and large file downloads.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **DSL (Digital Subscriber Line)**

 
 
• DSL is a family of technologies that provide Internet access by transmitting digital data over the wires of a local telephone network.
 
• Unlike cable Internet, DSL operates on existing telephone lines and does not share bandwidth with neighbors.
 
 
 
• **Dial-up**
 
 
• Dial-up Internet access is a form of Internet access that uses the facilities of the public switched telephone network (PSTN) to establish a connection to an Internet service provider (ISP).
 
• It is significantly slower than both DSL and cable Internet.
 
 
 
• **Fiber-optic Internet**
 
 
• Fiber-optic Internet uses fiber-optic cables to transmit data at very high speeds, often faster than both DSL and cable Internet.
 
• It provides a more stable and reliable connection with higher bandwidth.
 
 
 
• **Coaxial Cables**
 
 
• Coaxial cables are a type of electrical cable consisting of a central conductor, an insulating layer, a metallic shield, and an outer insulating layer.
 
• They are commonly used for cable television and Internet services due to their ability to carry high-frequency signals with low interference.

questions.question: What is the role of routers in Internet architecture ?

options.text: To provide security for Internet connections
To receive and send data on computer networks.
To translate IP addresses into domain names
To connect devices to the Internet

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To receive and send data on computer networks.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Routers** are networking devices that forward data packets between computer networks.
 
• They perform traffic directing functions on the Internet and ensure that data sent from one network gets to the right destination.
 
• Routers operate at the **network layer** (Layer 3) of the OSI model, making decisions based on IP addresses.
 
• They connect different networks together, enabling communication between devices on different networks and managing traffic efficiently.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **IP Address:**

 
 
• An Internet Protocol (IP) address is a unique identifier assigned to each device connected to a computer network that uses the IP for communication.
 
• IP addresses are used by routers to determine the destination of data packets.
 
 
 
• **Domain Name System (DNS):**
 
 
• The DNS translates domain names (like www.example.com) into IP addresses that routers and switches can use to route packets.
 
• While crucial for user-friendly web navigation, translating IP addresses into domain names is not the primary function of routers.
 
 
 
• **Network Layer (Layer 3) of the OSI Model:**
 
 
• The network layer is responsible for the delivery of packets from the source host to the destination host based on their IP addresses.
 
• Routers are critical components at this layer, managing the path that data takes to reach its destination.
 
 
 
• **Switches vs. Routers:**
 
 
• While both switches and routers are used in network environments, they serve different purposes.
 
• Switches operate at the data link layer (Layer 2) and are used to connect devices within the same network, while routers operate at the network layer and are used to connect different networks.

questions.question: What is the primary differentiating factor between broadband and dialup connections offered by ISPs?

options.text: Dialup connections offer higher security levels than broadband.
Broadband provides faster internet speeds compared to dialup.
Dialup connections are wireless, while broadband requires wired connections.
Dialup offers unlimited data usage, unlike broadband.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Broadband provides faster internet speeds compared to dialup.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Broadband** connections offer significantly **higher data transfer speeds** compared to dialup connections, providing a more efficient and faster internet experience.
 
• Broadband internet is always on, meaning there is no need to dial in each time you want to connect to the internet, unlike dialup.
 
• Broadband allows for simultaneous use of internet and telephone services, whereas dialup uses the telephone line, making it unavailable for calls during internet usage.
 
• Broadband connections can support modern internet applications such as streaming, gaming, and large file downloads, which are difficult to manage on slower dialup connections.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dialup Connection:**

 
 
• Dialup connection uses a modem and a standard telephone line to connect to an ISP.
 
• Typical dialup speeds are up to 56 kbps, which is significantly slower than broadband.
 
• Dialup connections often experience busy signals and require manual connection setup each time.
 
 
 
• **Broadband Types:**
 
 
• DSL (Digital Subscriber Line): Utilizes existing telephone lines but offers higher speeds without tying up the phone line.
 
• Cable Internet: Uses the cable television infrastructure to provide high-speed internet access.
 
• Fiber Optic: Provides the fastest internet speeds by using light to transmit data through fiber optic cables.
 
• Satellite Internet: Uses satellite communication for internet access, useful in remote areas.
 
 
 
• **Latency:**
 
 
• Latency refers to the delay in data transmission. Broadband connections generally have lower latency compared to dialup.
 
• Lower latency is crucial for real-time applications such as video conferencing and online gaming.
 
 
 
• **Data Cap and Unlimited Plans:**
 
 
• Broadband plans may come with data caps or unlimited data usage options, offering flexibility based on user needs.
 
• Dialup connections typically offer unlimited usage but are limited by slow speeds.
